plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack) based on iteration_16 results showing best_target_score of 0.909. Following feedback directives: (1) apply targeted cross-layer perturbation to asymmetric elements at layers 11, 15, 19, 20 with ±12% amplitude scaling, (2) switch optimizer annealing schedule to slower learning-rate decay factor 0.98. Three complementary routes proposed: Route 1 implements the exact feedback directive with focused perturbation bounds, Route 2 extends perturbation to additional transition-region layers with same annealing change, Route 3 tests multi-start initialization from iteration_16 best candidate with the new annealing schedule. All routes maintain 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology on fused silica substrate, normal incidence, dual-band objectives.

routes.title: Targeted Asymmetric-Layer Perturbation with Slower Annealing
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The four most asymmetric layers (11, 15, 19, 20) in the 24-layer dichroic stack dominate the shallow gradient region behavior; applying ±12% targeted perturbation bounds to these layers while maintaining broader bounds elsewhere, combined with slower annealing decay (0.98), will enable the optimizer to escape local minima and improve dual-band spectral separation.
routes.design_principle: Localized thickness freedom at transition-critical layers preserves the established high-performing stack structure while allowing fine-tuning where spectral band edges are most sensitive. Slower annealing maintains optimization momentum through shallow gradient regions identified in iteration_16.

routes.title: Extended Transition-Region Perturbation with Slower Annealing
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The transition region between visible-reflectance and IR-transmittance bands spans more than four layers; extending targeted perturbation to layers 10-12, 14-16, 18-20 (the central transition block) with ±15% bounds will capture additional degrees of freedom for band-edge optimization while slower annealing (0.98) maintains search momentum.
routes.design_principle: Broader transition-region perturbation acknowledges that spectral band edges are controlled by multiple adjacent layers rather than isolated asymmetric elements. The ±15% range provides more exploration freedom than route_02_refine_01 while still focusing search on physically critical regions.

routes.title: Multi-Start Initialization with Slower Annealing
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The optimization landscape contains multiple local minima near the iteration_16 solution; using multi-start initialization from iteration_16 top-3 candidates with the new annealing schedule (0.98) will identify whether a better global minimum exists within the same bounds, independent of perturbation strategy.
routes.design_principle: Multi-start optimization decouples the annealing improvement from the perturbation hypothesis, testing whether slower annealing alone improves convergence when starting from multiple high-quality initial points. This isolates the annealing effect from the layer-selection effect.
